applied_while_pending.description: Message says a change was already made although it still needs the user's confirmation.

capability_assumption.description: Asks for or promises a capability that configs/product_capabilities.yaml marks planned or unsupported (POL-A).

capacity_mismatch.description: Planned durations do not fit (or wildly underuse) weekly hours x horizon.

change_without_consent.description: Moderate/major change or removal applied without asking.

deadline_change_without_consent.description: A deadline changes without the autonomy POL-C allows (goal dates need confirmation; every change declares its autonomy).

en_third_person_pronoun.description: A gendered third-person pronoun in an English output — check it does not refer to the user or to someone whose pronouns are unknown.

generic_rationale.description: why_it_matters / reason uses a stock phrase that carries no task-specific reason.

novel_quantity.description: A quantity with a unit (hours, weeks, %, money) in user-facing text does not appear in the input; confirm it is derived correctly.

past_weekend_day.description: Plans a day of 'this weekend' that is already in the past relative to `today`.

promises_later_message.description: Promises to send something in a later message — requires a product capability.

retrieved_memory_leak.description: Distinctive words/numbers from another goal's retrieved memory appear in the output.

ru_gendered_identity_label.description: A Russian level/achievement title labels the user with a grammatically gendered noun/adjective.

ru_gendered_memory_input.description: Stored user memory in the input describes the user with a gendered form.

ru_gendered_self_reference.description: The assistant refers to itself with a gendered Russian form (e.g. 'разбил', 'я проверил').

ru_gendered_user_address.description: The user is addressed with a gendered Russian form (e.g. 'вы один', 'вы готов').

ru_informal_address.description: Informal 'ты' in a user-facing answer (product register is 'вы').

sensitive_memory_unflagged.description: Stored memory about health/caregiving/finances is marked sensitive: false.

tiny_goal_overplanned.description: A tiny goal gets more than 4 tasks/nodes.

too_many_questions.description: More than 3 clarification questions, or several questions in a non-clarification answer.

unsupported_feasibility_claim.description: Asserts that a date/target still works without the current-state facts needed to know it.

unsupported_generalisation.description: Confident generalisation about people/markets/institutions without a source.

unverifiable_criterion.description: An acceptance criterion the navigator cannot actually check from the evidence it asks for.

user_entered_as_objective.description: The protocol's ceiling exceeds what its required evidence classes support (POL-B: user-entered data is the user's word).

vague_node_title.description: Task/outline/added node title is generic (no object or quantity); outline titles are not linted.

weekday_date_mismatch.description: A weekday named together with a date does not match the calendar.

known_issues.description: «позвоню в воскресенье 5-го» — 5 October 2026 is a Monday (today is Sunday 27 September). The milestone move to 14 October is stated in decision_summary.impact but is not part of proposed_changes.
known_issues.proposed_revision: «позвоню в понедельник, 5-го» (or Sunday 4 October); add the milestone m1 date change to proposed_changes or drop it from the summary.
known_issues.found_by: agent inspection (confirmed by the weekday_date_mismatch audit rule)
known_issues.triage: Corrected in dataset v0.1.1; see the revision ledger entry.

known_issues.description: «about 140 hours of remaining work … around 11 months» counts the already verified project 1 (1,500 min). Remaining work is n2+n3+n4+n5+n6 = 6,900 min ≈ 115 h ≈ 38 weeks (≈ 9 months) at 3 h/week. The alternative's why_not («too late for the job search you planned») assumes a job search although the user has just accepted a job.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Use ≈115 h / ≈9 months in the message, decision_summary.why and the alternative; replace the job-search rationale with the user's stated purpose, or ask what the portfolio is for now.
known_issues.triage: Corrected in dataset v0.1.1; see the revision ledger entry.

known_issues.description: After 18 October the plan leaves chapter 3 (720 min) + chapter 4 (1,200 min) = 32 h at 4 h/week ≈ 8 weeks (≈ 13 December); even using the unused vacation hours it is ≈ 29 November. Moving milestone m1 to 22 November and «about three extra weeks of buffer» are not supported. The original 10 December milestone was itself infeasible (55 h at 4 h/week ≈ 31 December), which the answer should surface. new_weekly_hours_planned: 15 although the plan returns to 4 h/week after 18 October (the schema cannot express a temporary pace).
known_issues.proposed_revision: Recompute the milestone (≈ early–mid December), state that the vacation recovers the previously missing time rather than creating buffer, and resolve the temporary-pace representation (see schema weakness S2 in docs/DATASET_AUDIT_v0.1.0.md).
known_issues.triage: Corrected in dataset v0.1.1; see the revision ledger entry.

known_issues.description: «в плане — примерно 60 [часов]» is not derivable from the input: no node has a duration, and the original pacing (10 h × 11 weeks) implies ≈110 h of capacity. The ≈30 h available until 12 December is correct.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Add estimated_duration_minutes to the input nodes so that the remaining total is grounded, or phrase the comparison without a number.
known_issues.triage: Corrected in dataset v0.1.1; see the revision ledger entry.

known_issues.description: Pacing says 10 h/week × 22 weeks (220 h) and the message says «в темпе 10 часов в неделю», but estimated tasks total ≈47 h (job-search nodes unestimated); milestone m1 (4 weeks ≈ 40 h of capacity) contains ≈14 h of tasks. Achievement a4 «Первое собеседование» unlocks on completing n14 («20 откликов и 3 собеседования»), i.e. after the third interview.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Rebalance milestone dates or explain where the remaining weekly time goes; attach a4 to a node that represents the first interview.
known_issues.triage: Not changed in v0.1.1: rebalancing the milestone capacity and moving achievement a4 to a first-interview node is a product-content decision for a reviewer. J_MILESTONE_OVERBOOKED does not fire (the problem is under-booking, not over-booking).

known_issues.problem: F dependency / E realism / I user agency
known_issues.description: Mentor session 2 (n6) depends on n4 (3 run-throughs), which depends on the final deck (m1 target 25 October) — but the sessions are only offered in October, leaving about 6 days; «Сроки не меняются» ignores this. «Экономия около 7 часов» counts only the 450-min cut in n2 and ignores the 2 added mentor hours (net ≈5.5 h). Cutting n2 from 20 to 5 decks is applied as a 'minor' change without asking.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Make the October window explicit (e.g. session 2 on a draft run-through), state the net saving, and ask before reducing the user's planned task.
known_issues.triage: Corrected in dataset v0.1.1; see the revision ledger entry.

known_issues.description: Asks the user to import 18 months of shop sales data into an unspecified «free browser-based SQL sandbox»; sales exports often contain customer names and addresses. The COUNT(*) check compares two numbers that are both reported by the user, yet the ceiling is 'high'.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Use a local SQLite tool (or remove personal columns before any upload); make the check compare against something the user cannot simply type (e.g. the file's line count shown in the tool) or lower the ceiling.
known_issues.triage: Corrected in dataset v0.1.1; see the revision ledger entry.

known_issues.description: Level titles label the user with masculine forms: «Любитель доставки», «Уверенный нарезчик», «Домашний повар», «Хозяин ужина». A policy for gendered identity labels in Russian does not exist yet. Achievement a1 «Первое блюдо своими руками» unlocks on the first verified task, which is knife practice, not a dish.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Gender-neutral titles naming the stage rather than the person (e.g. «Уверенная нарезка», «Домашняя кухня», «Ужин для друзей»); attach a1 to the first dish (n5) or rename it.
known_issues.triage: Level titles are accepted under POL-D rule 3 (badge names may use natural role nouns); achievement a1 renamed because it unlocked on a technique, not a dish.

known_issues.description: Verification relies on capabilities that no spec defines: issuing a random scramble (vprot-001), calling the user's API endpoints (vprot-003), the AI opening links (vprot-004), automatic transcription and timing of audio (task-002), and sending control tasks in a later message (vres-002, ev-vr-01). If the product lacks them, the model learns to promise features that do not exist.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Product owner publishes the capability list (docs + navigator prompt); revise the examples to match it.
known_issues.triage: Fixed in gj-vprot-001 (no video), gj-vprot-003 (no API calls) and gj-vres-002 (no later message). gj-vprot-004 (fetching submitted links) and gj-task-002 (audio transcript) use capabilities declared available — resolved by policy. ev-vr-01 stays as it is: evaluation v0.1.0 is frozen and superseded by v0.2.0, where capability promises are checked (capability_compliance).

known_issues.problem: P2 verification (user-entered data treated as objective)
known_issues.location: verification protocols with only structured_result required
known_issues.description: Protocols whose only required evidence is user-entered (structured_result, sometimes + follow_up_questions) are not self_report_only and have a 'medium' or 'high' ceiling. Sometimes that is defensible (rows carry links or quotes), sometimes it is not (e.g. gj-jour-002 n3 capacity, gj-task-004 n1-t3 repairs). There is no rule for when structured user data may exceed 'limited'.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Decide a policy, e.g. «structured_result alone → limited, unless every row carries an externally checkable reference (URL, document, third-party message)»; then re-rate these protocols.
known_issues.triage: Every listed protocol re-rated under POL-B: lowered to limited, given checkable references with a URL check, or declared an inspectable artifact with a reason.

known_issues.triage: Needs medical/dietetic expert sign-off (expert tier).

known_issues.description: «объём придётся наращивать быстрее, чем обычно советуют, а это главный риск травм» is a sports-medicine generalisation; classifying a marathon in 17 weeks from 10 km/week as 'allowed' rather than 'sensitive' is debatable.

known_issues.triage: Needs sports-medicine expert sign-off of the claim and of the safety category.

known_issues.problem: L external-fact discipline / K explanation quality (overclaiming)
known_issues.description: Confident generalisations without a source: «many analyst roles value exactly that domain knowledge», «those two sections are what the demo-day judges decide on», «everything a hiring manager looks for», «ценнее любого количества чужих деков», «работает хуже любого, который вам нравится», «booking months ahead usually keeps them within budget», «на нём чаще всего спотыкаются». How much general knowledge the navigator may assert is not specified.
known_issues.proposed_revision: Hedge or remove; add a rule to DATASET_SPEC on stable general knowledge vs. claims that need a source.
known_issues.triage: Partly addressed: the overclaims in gj-route-004 and gj-clar-007 were softened while those examples were revised. The rule on stable general knowledge vs. claims needing a source is still not specified; remaining instances stay for review.
